candidates.title: Classic nest
candidates.idea: Richard's idea drawn straight: Shelf's bookmark in paper, the largest play hole its walls allow, and a paper pause sitting on the play's incircle. The play is the dark tile showing through and the pause is the bookmark's own paper again, so one shape carries save, listen and pause.
candidates.built: Bookmark at Shelf's proportions, 43.5 dp wide with its top at 27.1, as large as the 66 dp safe circle allows (reach 32.6 dp). The play is equilateral, 38.3 dp tall, with its corners rounded at the bookmark's shoulder radius (5.1 dp); it is the largest that keeps at least 6 dp of paper round it: 6 at the top corner and over the notch, 8.2 on the left, 7.3 past the drawn tip. Its centroid sits 2.5 dp left of the centre line, which puts the drawn play's box 0.5 dp right of it, halfway between centroid and box centring; that is what looks centred inside a rectangle. The pause sits on the incircle (radius 11.05 dp): bars 3.4 x 11.4 dp, 3.1 dp apart, corner radius 1 dp, with 4 dp of dark to the slanted sides and 6.1 dp to the flat side. The extra on the flat side is deliberate: a gap that runs parallel to a bar looks narrower than the same gap at a corner. One even-odd path.
candidates.small: 48 px: bookmark 28 x 34 px, play 24 px tall with its sides at 4:7 (within a degree of equilateral) and r 3 corners, 3.8 to 5 px of paper round it. The pause is dropped there: once a 3 px ring and a 3 px gap come out of a play with a 7 px incircle, 3 px bars could only be about 4 px tall. 32 px: bookmark 20 x 24 px with a 16 px play and 3 to 4 px walls, no pause. 16 px: bookmark 10 x 12 px with a 4 x 7 px play drawn in whole pixels, so it stays crisp. Glyph 24: bookmark 16 x 20 px with a 12 px play hole and at least 3 px of white round it; no pause, since the media notification beside it already carries play and pause. The pause therefore lives only in the launcher icon and on the launch screens.
candidates.risks: Google Play Books also builds its icon from a bookmark-like shape round a play triangle; the pause island, the single colour and Shelf's square shoulders set this apart, and only the last two survive below 64 px. On a home screen at 1x the pause shrinks to two specks and the icon reads as a bookmark with a play button, which could suggest a podcast or video app. The toolbar cuts carry the play alone.
candidates.self_critique: Well made and faithful, but it is the drawing anyone would arrive at from Richard's sentence, so it is closer to forgettable than I would like. The pause exists only in the launcher icon: every toolbar cut and the glyph are bookmark plus play, which is exactly the Play Books composition. The equilateral play's lower side (30 degrees) runs nearly but not quite parallel to the notch (32.9), so the paper band under it tapers by about 1.5 dp: near-parallel lines that are not parallel are the kind of thing n3 fixes. The ring round the pause is uneven by design (4 dp to the slanted sides, 6.1 to the flat side); I think it reads as even, but someone measuring will see it. At 1x on a home screen it reads as a media button in a bookmark before it reads as reading.

candidates.title: Bookmark window
candidates.idea: The bookmark first: a smaller play hole set in Shelf's bookmark like a window, with a broad margin of paper all round and the paper pause held snugly inside it. Of the three it keeps the most solid bookmark, so saving reads before listening.
candidates.built: Same bookmark as n1 (43.5 dp wide, top at 27.1, reach 32.6 dp). The play is equilateral, 32.3 dp tall, corners at the shoulder radius, sized so at least 7.5 dp of paper stays round it: 7.5 over the notch, 9 at the top corner, 10.4 on the left and 10.2 past the drawn tip. The band over the notch is the thinnest on purpose, because the tails add paper either side of it. The play's centroid is at (52, 48.5), on the bookmark's visual centre, which sits lower than the middle of the body above the notch; centred on the body, the play looked high. The pause sits on the incircle (radius 9.3 dp): bars 3.3 x 10 dp, 2.8 dp apart, inside a 3 dp ring, tighter than n1's 4 dp, so the island keeps its size in the smaller play.
candidates.small: 48 px: bookmark 28 x 34 px with a 20 px play and 4.8 to 7 px of paper round it; no pause, as the play's incircle is under 6 px in radius. 32 px: a 14 px play with 3.4 to 5 px of paper; no pause. 16 px: the same 4 x 7 px stepped play as n1. Glyph 24: an 11 px play hole with at least 3.3 px of white round it; no pause. In the 48, the 32 and the glyph the play's ends sit on half pixels so the paper above and below it keeps the master's ratio; the play has no level edge, so nothing blurs.
candidates.risks: The quietest of the three, and the nearest to a bookmark with a play badge placed on it, the clip-art reading the brief warns against. Its pause is the smallest here and turns to specks on a 1x home screen, and its play window is small in the 32 and 16 px cuts. It shares n1's likeness to Google Play Books, at a lower volume.
candidates.self_critique: This is the replacement for the stencil, and it is n1 at a lower volume: the same construction with a smaller window, so the difference is one of hierarchy, not of idea. It is worth showing only as the calm end of the range (bookmark first, n1 balanced, n3 play first). It has the least negative space of the three, which runs against Richard asking to play with negative space, and it is the one most open to the 'symbol stamped on a bookmark' criticism from the first round. Its pause (3.3 x 10 dp) is the smallest and the most at risk on a home screen. I would not put it forward as the answer.

candidates.title: One hand
candidates.idea: The play hole is cut at the notch's own angle, its two sides parallel to the notch's two diagonals, so tail and triangle look cut by one hand, and it is as large as the bookmark can hold. That leaves room for a full-height pause in an even dark ring, and one module sets every wall, bar and gap, so the pause survives down to 32 px.
candidates.built: Same bookmark (43.5 dp wide, top at 27.1, reach 32.6 dp). The play's sides slope at the notch's 11 in 17 (32.9 degrees from level, 65.8 at the tip), so it is 44.6 dp tall and 34.5 deep, corners at the shoulder radius. One module, 4.1 dp (9.4% of the bookmark's width), sets the paper band over the notch, which runs parallel to it, the top wall, both pause bars, the gap between them and the dark ring round them. The left wall, 6.8 dp, is the one measure off the module, chosen so the drawn tip sits 6.5 dp from the right edge and the play is optically centred. The bars come out at 4.1 x 14.6 dp, about 1 to 3.5, the proportion of a standard pause sign. The left bar is a module from the flat side and the right bar's corners a module from the slanted sides, so the ring is even on all three sides and the pause sits in the deep part of the play, 1.9 dp left of the incircle centre.
candidates.small: The module is 3 px on the 48 px cut and 2 px on the 32, so both keep the pause. 48 px: bookmark 32 x 40 px, a 33 px play and 3 x 9 px bars, with the notch and the play's sides at 2:3 so they stay parallel on the pixel grid. 32 px: bookmark 22 x 27 px, a 23 px play and 2 x 6 px bars. Every bar sits on whole pixels. To make room, these two bookmarks fill about two thirds of the tile, against the master's 60%. 16 px drops the pause, since a 1 px module blurs into one grey patch, and shares n1's 4 x 7 px stepped play. Glyph 24: bookmark 16 x 20 px with a 15 px play hole and 2 px walls; no pause, as a 2 px pause does not fit.
candidates.risks: The hole is so large that the bookmark becomes a frame, and at a glance the play can register before the bookmark; that also puts it closest of the three to Google Play Books. The walls are 4.1 dp, under 3 px on a 1x home screen, so the frame looks light beside solid icons. The small cuts are drawn larger in their tiles than the master, so in the toolbar the icon looks a size up from the launcher's proportions.
candidates.self_critique: The strongest of the three and the one I would show: every diagonal shares the notch's angle, one module drives walls, bars, gap and ring, the pause has a real pause's proportions, and it is the only nest whose pause is still there in the 48 and 32 px toolbar cuts. What still bothers me: the play is so dominant that the icon can read as a play button in a bookmark-shaped frame, which is both the Play Books risk and a 'video or music app first' risk; the frame is thin (4.1 dp) and looks light beside solid launcher icons at 1x; the one-module story has one exception (the 6.8 dp left wall, needed for optical centring); the pause is fitted into the deep part of the play rather than centred on the incircle, which some eyes will read as sitting left; the 48 and 32 cuts only keep the pause because their bookmarks are drawn about 10% larger in the tile than the master; and the 16 px cut, shared with n1 and n2, loses everything that makes n3 distinct.

candidates.title: Centred play
candidates.idea: Shelf's bookmark in solid paper with one hole: an equilateral play, rounded as softly as the bookmark's shoulders and set in the middle of the body, so the paper around it reads as an even frame. The bookmark reads first, and the hole says every save can be played.
candidates.built: Bookmark 42.5 dp wide, 1.25 times today's with its proportions unchanged, drawn box centred on the canvas; the farthest ink is 32.4 dp from the centre. In bookmark units (34 wide): the play is 22 tall and 19.05 deep (equilateral), half the bookmark's height. Corners r 2.5 units (3.1 dp): on a 60 degree corner that reads as soft as the 4 unit shoulders on their 90. The flat side sits 0.42 of the play's depth left of the centre line, between box centring (0.5) and centroid centring (0.33), leaving 9 units of paper at the flat side and 8.45 at the rounded tip, which look equal. The play's axis is 17.25 units below the top: 8.1 units of paper above the hole and 6.4 to the notch's apex, which balances because the apex is a point. The hole is 16% of the bookmark's area.
candidates.small: 48 px: bookmark 28 x 34 px with a 9 px notch; the play 18 x 16 px with its flat side on x 17, 7 px of paper at the flat side and at the tip, 6.5 px above and 5.2 to the apex. 32 px: bookmark 18 x 22, play 11 x 9.5 px on x 12, walls of 5 and 4.9 px, 4.5 above and 3.3 to the apex. 16 px: bookmark 10 x 12; the play is redrawn in whole pixels as columns of 5, 3, 3 and 1 on x 6, rows 4 to 8, floating with 2 px of paper above and 2 to 3 below, since a drawn triangle this small is only grey pixels. Glyph: bookmark 16 x 20, play 10 px tall on x 8 with 4 px walls. Every cut keeps the play; nothing is dropped.
candidates.risks: Google Play Books pairs the same two symbols, a soft play triangle holding a bookmark. Here the silhouette is Shelf's square-shouldered bookmark and the play is a hole, which keeps them apart, but a bigger or softer play would close the gap. After the silhouette, the play is the loudest thing on the icon, so among media apps it could be taken for a player. At 16 px the play is 5 px tall and only just reads as a play.
candidates.self_critique: It is the expected answer: a play set in a bookmark, carefully proportioned (walls measured, not eyeballed) but with no idea beyond the symbol itself, so it sits close to the clip-art reading the brief warns about. At launcher sizes it is hard to tell from p2 without looking. A soft rounded play next to a bookmark is Google Play Books' pairing reversed, which nags. The 16 px play is 5 px tall and only just a play. The 42.5 dp bookmark sits closer to the circle mask's edge than the reference (3.6 dp clearance against 5.3), slightly tight in the circle at 48 px.

candidates.title: Notch-cut play
candidates.idea: The two cuts that make the bookmark's tail, folded to point forward, make the play: its slanted edges run parallel to the notch's and are just as long, so the hole and the tail look cut by the same hand. The play rests on the tail with an even strap of paper along the notch, and its angle is also the angle of the play button inside the app.
candidates.built: Bookmark as p1: 42.5 dp wide, today's proportions, drawn box centred. The play is the notch's triangle folded: its flat side is twice the notch's depth (22 units of 34, 27.5 dp) and its depth half the bookmark's width (17 units, 21.25 dp), so both slanted edges have the notch's slope (32.9 degrees) and length (20.25 units), and the hole has the notch's area. The prototype's Lucide play (polygon 6 3, 20 12, 6 21) slopes at 32.7 degrees, so it is the same shape. Corners r 1.5 units (1.9 dp), the tail tips' radius, because the play's back corners have the tips' 57 degree angle. The flat side sits 0.46 of the depth left of the centre line, leaving 9.2 units of paper at the flat side and 9.1 at the tip. The lower edge is set 5 units square to the notch's left edge: a strap thinner than the 9.2 to 9.4 units at the flat side, tip and top, so the play reads as resting on the tail. The hole is 14.8% of the bookmark.
candidates.small: Each cut builds the play from its own notch, so the edges stay parallel to the notch at every size. 48 px: notch 9 over 14, play 18 x 14 px with its flat side on x 18 (8 px of paper there, 7 at the tip), strap 4 px, 6.6 px above. 32 px: notch 6 over 9, play 12 x 9 px on x 12, strap 2.6 px. 16 px: the play is redrawn in whole pixels as columns of 6, 4, 4 and 2 on x 6, rows 4 to 9, resting on the tail with 2 px above and its lower steps 1 to 2 px from the notch. Glyph: notch 5 over 8, play 10 x 8 px on x 8, strap 3 px. Every cut keeps the play.
candidates.risks: The crisp corners follow the tail tips, so they are much crisper than the round shoulders, and some will read them as sharp. The play sits below the middle on purpose, which out of context can look as if it has slipped. At launcher sizes the difference from p1 is subtle (narrower, crisper, lower), and the notch rhyme is only visible from about 48 px up. Google Play Books pairs the same two symbols; the bookmark silhouette and the hole keep them apart.
candidates.self_critique: The strongest idea of the three, and the construction is real rather than claimed: the play's edges are the notch's edges in slope and length, it has the notch's area, and it matches the angle of the in-app play button. But below 48 px nobody will see the construction; on a home screen it reads as a slightly narrower, lower, crisper p1. The 1.9 dp corners break the brief's 'about the shoulder radius' default on purpose. At 288 px they read as cut rather than sharp, but Richard rejected sharp triangles last time and may not see the distinction. The 48 px cut cannot centre the play exactly (8 px of paper at the flat side against 7 at the tip) without a half-pixel flat side, because its depth is locked to the notch's half-width. The 16 px play's tip is 2 px wide and blunt.

candidates.title: Quiet play
candidates.idea: The bookmark stays the hero, with the app's own play button punched small through its optical centre. The icon says saved first and listen second.
candidates.built: Bookmark as p1: 42.5 dp wide, today's proportions, drawn box centred. The play has the proportions of the player's Lucide play (14 deep by 18 tall); its flat side is 15 units of 34 (18.75 dp), 36% of the bookmark's height, the smallest play a 48 px icon still shows without effort. Corners r 1.7 units, 0.11 of its height, the same softness as p1's play. The flat side sits 0.40 of the depth left of the centre line, close to centroid centring, because the eye places a small shape in a wide field by its mass. The axis is 17.6 units below the top: the centre of mass is at 18.4, but a small play there reads low. Walls: 12.3 units at the flat side, 11.4 at the tip, 11.5 above and 7.8 to the notch's apex. The hole is 6.6% of the bookmark.
candidates.small: 48 px: play 12 x 9.3 px on x 20, 10 px of paper at the flat side and 9.9 at the tip. 32 px: play 8.5 x 6.6 px on x 13, walls of 6 and 6.2 px. 16 px: the play in whole pixels as columns of 5, 3 and 1 on x 7, rows 5 to 9, the smallest shape that still reads as a play. Glyph: play 8.5 px tall on x 9, walls of 5 and 5.2 px. Every cut keeps the play; at 16 px it is as tall as p1's, as nothing smaller reads as a play.
candidates.risks: The least inventive of the three: a symbol set into the bookmark, close to clip art, kept clear of it only by its restraint. The play is small, so in the status bar and at 16 px it is a 5 px mark that can be taken for a speck, and on a busy home screen the listen message is easy to miss. It shares its play shape with p2.
candidates.self_critique: Competent but forgettable. It exists because every bolder third idea failed (see dropped), and it is the only one that keeps saved first and listen second at real sizes. The negative space does nothing beyond carrying the symbol, which is the clip-art failure the brief names, softened only by its size. Its play shape is p2's at two thirds the size, so the family has two near-relatives. The quiet idea does not survive at 16 px, where the play has to be as tall as p1's to read at all.

candidates.title: Split bookmark
candidates.idea: Shelf's bookmark cut once down its centre line, so the two halves stand as a pause sign. Each half keeps its half of the notch, and the eye closes the two slopes back into one bookmark; a pause and a bookmark both mean stop here and come back later.
candidates.built: geom.bookmark at 42 dp wide with today's proportions, drawn as one compound path of two pieces, centred on its drawn box (reach 32.0 of the 33 dp safe radius, centroid 1.9 dp above centre). The cut is 6.3 dp, 0.15 of the width. The app's own pause button (Lucide pause filled with the 1.75 stroke: bars 5.75 wide, gap 2.25) has a gap of 0.164 of its width; a hair narrower here lets the bookmark lead, and from 0.18 up the halves start to read as two separate bars. Each half runs from its tip up its half of the notch to the cut, so the slope is unbroken. The four corners the cut makes take the tip radius (1.5/34 of the width) and only the outer shoulders are round, so the halves read as one shape cut through.
candidates.small: Nothing is dropped at any size. 48 px: 28 x 34 px, 4 px cut, shoulders r 3, each notch edge from the tip at (10, 41) to the cut at (22, 33), a 2:3 slope close to the master's. 32 px: 20 x 24 px with a 4 px cut, since a 2 px cut went faint where this size shows at 16 CSS px on 2x screens; notch 5 over 8. 16 px: 10 x 12 px, 2 px cut, notch 3 over 4, shoulders r 1. I tried 1:2 slopes at 48 and 32: cleaner steps, but visibly flatter than the master's notch and no fewer grey pixels. Glyph: 16 x 20 px with a 2 px cut, the master's proportion, because phones draw it at 2.6 times or more.
candidates.risks: It reads as a pause sign, and as listening only to someone who already knows Shelf reads articles aloud; pause on its own says something is playing now. Out of context, most of all at 16 px, it can pass for a media app's pause button before it reads as a bookmark; the angled feet keep it Shelf's. Near lookalikes: a Roman numeral II, a parallel sign. The gap carries the whole idea, so every later redraw has to keep it open.
candidates.self_critique: The strongest of my three and the one I would show Richard. Its soft-pixel share is lower than the solid reference's at every size (2.8, 5.1 and 11.4 per cent against 3.5, 6.3 and 14.7). Out of context it can still read as a media pause button before a bookmark, and at 16 px the bookmark survives only through three pixels of slope on each foot. The notch's apex, the bookmark's most recognisable point, is gone and has to be inferred by the eye. The mark becomes two pieces, so any one-colour use (print, emboss, stitch) must keep the gap open. The gap's share of the width drifts with the pixel grid (0.15 master, 0.14 at 48, 0.2 at 32 and 16, 0.125 on the glyph). I chose 0.15 by eye over the app pause's 0.164; the difference is under a dp and could go either way.

candidates.title: Forked tail
candidates.idea: Shelf's bookmark with its notch carried up the centre line as a slot, so the tail forks into two legs under a whole head. It was meant to be a bookmark and a pause at once; drawn, it reads as a bookmark with a split tail, and the pause does not come through.
candidates.built: The same 42 dp bookmark and 6.3 dp cut as s1 (0.15 of the width), stopped 0.4 of the height below the top edge: the slot rises 17.5 dp above the notch's apex, and its corners take the tip radius. I drew heads of 0.45, 0.4, 0.33, 0.3, 0.24, 0.16 and 0.1 of the height, slots from 0.1 to 0.22 of the width, and square, round and pointed slot ends. From about 0.33 down the shape reads as a Π, a gate or a pair of trousers, so 0.4 is the deepest that is still plainly the bookmark.
candidates.small: Nothing is dropped. 48 px: 28 x 34 px, a 4 px slot from the notch up to y 21, leaving 14 px of head. 32 px: 20 x 24 px, 4 px slot up to y 14. 16 px: 10 x 12 px, 2 px slot up to y 7. Glyph: 16 x 20 px, 2 px slot up to y 10. The head is about 0.4 of the height at every size, and the notch edges use s1's slopes.
candidates.risks: It reads as neither a pause nor listening. Any bridge across the top, however thin, joins the legs into one letter-like object (Π, a gate, trousers), and Shelf's bookmark is too short for its legs to pass as pause bars: cut all the way through, each half is about 2.8 times as tall as it is wide, and every bit of head left on makes the legs stubbier. The dark slot and notch together can look like an upside-down Y, a crack or a rocket's fins. It answers how deep the slot can go; I would not put it forward on its own.
candidates.self_critique: It does not do what it was asked to do. No depth of slot makes the legs read as a pause: any bridge turns two bars into one letter-like shape, and the bookmark's proportions leave the legs too stubby. It is a carefully drawn negative result (crisp cuts, 2.6 per cent soft at 48), kept so Richard can see that s1's cut has to go all the way through. The dark slot-and-notch shape means nothing for Shelf and can read as a crack. I looked hard for a better replacement in the territory (listed under dropped) and found none that beat it on the brief's own terms, so I left the honest answer in place.

candidates.title: Notch-echo pause
candidates.idea: A solid Shelf bookmark with a pause cut out of its body. The two holes together are the bookmark's own outline, inset and cut down the middle, so the pause stands on the tail's angle and the paper under it is an even chevron.
candidates.built: The 42 dp bookmark as in s1. Two holes 8 dp wide with a 4 dp spine between them (half a hole, as tight as the app's own pause button). Paper: 11 dp at the sides, 10.5 above, and 9 dp between the holes and the notch measured square to the notch edge, so the chevron band is even along its length. The holes sit wholly above the notch's apex, and their corners take the tip radius. With 9 dp walls the paper turned into a frame, close to the outlined bookmark that means not saved in most interfaces; with 12 dp walls the holes started to look like a pair of eyes.
candidates.small: Nothing is dropped. 48 px: 28 x 34 px; holes 5 px wide, a 4 px spine and 7 px walls, the holes' bottoms 3 px lower at the outside edge (the echo). 32 px: 20 x 24 px; holes 4 px, spine 2, walls 5, a 2 px echo. 16 px: 10 x 12 px; holes, spine and walls 2 px each, with flat bottoms, since a one-pixel slant only adds grey. Glyph: 16 x 20 px; holes 4 px, spine 2, side walls 3, top 4, a 2 px echo.
candidates.risks: The most literal of the three: a pause stamped into a bookmark, the same construction as Google Play Books (a media symbol inside a bookmark-like shape) with pause in place of play. It reads as a pause sign, and as listening only to someone who knows Shelf reads aloud. The echo is quiet at 48 px and gone at 16. Two dark slots in a light shape can read as eyes; the narrow spine and the holes' height hold it to a pause.
candidates.self_critique: Competent and legible at every size, but literal. It is a symbol in a bookmark, which is what the first attempt was criticised for and how Google Play Books is built. The inset-and-split logic and the notch echo are the only things tying the pause to the bookmark, and the echo is quiet at 48 px and gone at 16. The pause is smaller and weaker than s1's, and at 16 px the holes are 2 px slits. The 32 px cut is softer than the reference (9.6 against 6.3 per cent) because of the hole bottoms' diagonals.

candidates.title: The notch plays
candidates.idea: Shelf's bookmark laid on its side, tail to the left, so the notch it already has points right as a play button. One solid shape with no holes: the play is the space the bookmark's own tail leaves open.
candidates.built: Today's bookmark turned a quarter turn clockwise, 37 dp wide (its height on the tile) and 54.8 long. The notch is deepened from 11/34 of the width to 14/18, the proportion of Shelf's in-app play icon (Lucide play: 18 tall, 14 deep), so the notch and the player's play are the same triangle. In a depth study (0.55, 0.62, 0.70, 0.78) the dark wedge read as a chevron up to 0.62 and as a play from 0.70, most firmly at 0.78. The body behind the apex is 26 dp, 0.7 of the width. Corner radii follow the bookmark: shoulders 4/34 of the width, tips 1.5/34, and the notch's apex takes the shoulder radius (4.35 dp) so the play's point is as soft as the shoulders. Centred on y 54. Horizontally the notch takes weight from the left, so the box is moved left of centre by 0.65 of the gap between its box centre and its centroid: box-centred looked right-heavy, centroid-centred pushed the tips past the safe circle. Reach 32.6 dp, inside the 33 dp circle.
candidates.small: Every size keeps the whole drawing, because there is nothing inside to drop. 48 px: 24 x 34 px, the notch 18 deep on a 2 : 3 staircase (the nearest clean slope to the play's 0.78), shoulders r 3, the apex r 3 (the master's 4.35 dp is 2.9 px here), sharp tips. 32 px: 16 x 23, notch 12, shoulders r 2, apex r 1. 16 px: 8 x 11, notch 6, shoulders r 1, sharp apex, 2 px clear on the left and 3 on the right. Each cut's body is the master's at that scale, so the mark sits where the master does. Glyph: 14 x 20 in the 20 px box, an 11 px notch (11/14, the play's ratio again) with its apex on a whole pixel.
candidates.risks: On its side the bookmark loses the hang that makes it a bookmark: it can read as a tag, a label, a pennant or the tail of an arrow first, and its square shoulders are the only cue left, small at 48 px. Gmail's 'important' marker is a horizontal tag with a notched end, and Plex's chevron sits close to the notch's outline on a dark tile. A bookmark paired with a play triangle is Google Play Books' ground, which the brief flags; here the play is empty space on a sideways shape, but the pairing is the same. The play is a figure-ground switch: some people will see a chevron bite or a forward arrow until it is pointed out. The deeper notch makes the prongs long and pointed, so it is further from today's chunky bookmark than any upright option.
candidates.self_critique: Next to the upright reference on sheets/tail.png, it reads as a tag, label or pennant before a bookmark. Laying it on its side trades the bookmark's hang for the play, and no notch depth or body length recovers both. I tried D/W from 0.32 to 0.87 and bodies from 24 to 36; long reads as a banner, short as a ticket. The 14/18 notch is far from Shelf's shallow one, with long pointed prongs. At 1x on the home screen the notch reads as a chevron bite before it reads as a play. In its favour, it is the purest negative space in this territory: one shape, no holes, the play made by the bookmark's own tail. The themed icon, glyph and light colourway come free, and every cut is drawn by hand, at the reference's softness (48/32/16 px soft 4.6/7.8/14.7%, against 3.5/6.3/14.7). Reviewer note: the rejected first round had this premise inside its 'Swallowtail' option, so Richard has seen the sideways-notch idea before, drawn badly. This is it redrawn with Shelf's shoulders, a measured notch and tuned cuts. Worth showing as the clean version of the idea; probably not the one.

candidates.title: Play, then pause
candidates.idea: t1's sideways bookmark with a pause cut through its body, so the notch is the play and two slots are the pause: both of Richard's symbols are negative space in one solid shape. A bookmark marks where you stopped; here its tail resumes and its body pauses.
candidates.built: t1's bookmark exactly (37 dp wide, the notch 14/18 of the width as Shelf's in-app play icon, the same corner radii, the apex at the shoulder radius), with the body behind the apex lengthened from 26 to 29.5 dp to hold the pause. candidates.title: Paused bookmark

candidates.risks: The paper disc makes this the brightest icon on a dark home screen and moves it away from the dark icon Richard described; it is 42% paper against the solid reference's 33%. A light disc with a dark mark can read as a button, and the pause could suggest a media app at a glance, although the bookmark's square shoulders and notch read first at launcher sizes. A bookmark in a circle also echoes Telegram's Saved Messages avatar, a white bookmark on a blue disc. The pause is gone at 16 px and in the glyph, so the toolbar and the status bar show a plain bookmark disc.
candidates.self_critique: It is the stronger of my two and well drawn: today's bookmark at today's size, two radii in the whole drawing, the pause placed by eye after three position tests, and every cut hand-placed on whole pixels. The 16 px cut is crisper than the solid reference (6.5% soft against 14.7). What still bothers me: (1) The swap costs the dark icon Richard asked for. A 64 dp paper disc makes it the brightest thing on a dark home screen. (2) Both levels really are negative space, yet the finished picture can still be summed up as 'a bookmark with a pause in it', which is close to the 'symbol stamped in a bookmark' the first round was rejected for. The light colourway reads that way most of all. (3) A disc round a mark reads as a button or badge, and the pause adds a media flavour, so it sits nearer a podcast-app look than ref-solid does. (4) The listening idea only exists at launcher sizes and in the 48 and 32 px cuts. At 16 px and in the glyph it becomes a plain bookmark disc. (5) The 48 and 32 px cuts are softer than the reference (11.6% and 17.7%) because a circle's rim cannot sit on whole pixels. Next to ref-solid on the comparison sheet it is bolder and says more, but it is less calm and less ownable.

candidates.risks: It is the most literal option: a page with a bookmark is a familiar 'bookmarked document' pictogram, so it relies on Shelf's square shoulders and shallow notch to be its own. It says nothing about listening. A light portrait card on a dark tile could be taken for a phone or a cards app at a glance. The page is narrower than a disc, so it looks slighter than its neighbours on a home screen (26% paper against the solid reference's 33%), and at 16 px it nearly fills the tile's height, with 1 px of tile above and below.
candidates.self_critique: Its craft is the best in my territory. Both levels survive at every size with nothing dropped, and the cuts are the crispest I drew (5% soft at 48 and 32, 5.8% at 16, against ref-solid's 14.7 at 16). It also settles one real question: hanging the bookmark from the page's head in an even margin is what turns a 'frame' into a 'page'. Honestly, though, it is competent but forgettable. Next to ref-solid on the comparison sheet it looks like the reference's light colourway put onto a card, a stock 'bookmarked document' glyph with Shelf's notch. It drops Richard's play/pause entirely, it is slight on a home screen (26% paper), and at 16 px the page nearly fills the tile's height. I kept it because it is genuinely different from i1 (a different field, a different metaphor, two levels), and because it shows whether the swap can carry Shelf with the bookmark alone. I would not put it in front of Richard ahead of i1 or ref-solid.

At a glance that diagonal invites the 'slash' or folded-page reading. The play is paper, the reverse of Richard's dark play. The 3.2 dp cut becomes 2.1 px on a 1x home screen, which is visible but soft. And p2 (another designer) uses the same notch-angle insight as a centred play hole, so Richard will see the two as relatives: p2 states the play, h1 hides it in the tail.

It is three pieces where h1 is two. The back bookmark shows only its right half, so it reads as a bar, and the play looks placed under the front bookmark rather than discovered as the corner of a second one. Sliding the back bookmark until its notch showed fixed the reading but shrank the play to 8 x 6 px at 1x, and 3 px gaps at 48 px leave no play at all, so I chose the larger play over the clearer pair. Kept because it is the only true between-two-shapes play in this territory that no other designer covers. It is weaker than h1 by a clear margin.

candidates.title: Ribbon with a play
candidates.idea: Shelf's bookmark hangs from the top edge of the tile like the ribbon marker in a hardback, so the tile becomes the book and only the ribbon's body and notched tail show. A play is cut out of the body: kept for later, and ready to listen to.
candidates.built: Ribbon 40 dp wide (the solid reference's width), running from y 0 so it passes the top of every mask and the launcher's parallax, down to tips at y 79, with Shelf's notch (11/34 of the width, 12.9 dp) and tips r 1.76; the rounded tips reach 30.2 dp from the centre. The play's slanted edges are parallel to the notch's (tan 11/17), which makes it 24 dp tall and 18.5 deep, a little slimmer than equilateral; its two back corners then share the tips' 57 degrees, and the band of paper under it runs parallel to the notch. Corners r 1.76, like the tips. It sits 0.35 of the way from box centring to centroid centring, and its height is set by the 10.5 dp band under it, which puts its centre at y 46.9: walls 11.8 left, 11.1 right (to the rounded tip) and 10.5 under, measured square to the notch.
candidates.small: The cuts keep a lip of tile above the ribbon, 3 px at 48, 2 at 32 and 1 at 16, the smallest detail each size allows: bled to the edge, the paper merged with light browser toolbars and the tile read as a dark U. The ribbon's square top corners still say it comes from under the edge, and every cut keeps the play's rhyme with the notch. 48: ribbon 28 px, notch 9 px over a 14 px half width (Shelf's slope), play 17 px with its flat side on column 18; walls 8, 6.8 and 6.6 px. 32: ribbon 18 px, notch 6 px, play 12 px on column 12, a little larger than the master's so it holds on a 2x toolbar. 16: ribbon 8 px, notch 4 px at 45 degrees as in small.svg, play a 3 x 5 pixel staircase whose 45-degree steps match the notch, with its centroid on the centre line. candidates.risks: A bookmark with a play in it is close to Google Play Books. One colour, a modest hole and the ribbon running off the tile keep some distance, but this is the main risk. The bleed relies on the tile's edge being visible: on a wallpaper near graphite the ribbon's top reads as the bookmark's own, flat in the squircle and arched in the circle and teardrop; on a pale wallpaper the paper merges with the background, and the tile becomes a dark frame round a bookmark-shaped opening with the play floating in it, which still reads. The toolbar cuts need a lip of tile for the same reason, so they show the ribbon starting just under the edge. The launch screens and the website need an edge for the ribbon to hang from, such as the top of the screen; Android 12's circle-masked splash would cut it with the circle.
candidates.self_critique: Well made and legible at every size. The notch rhyme gives one angle system: the play's back corners equal the tips' 57.1 degrees and the band under it runs parallel to the notch. Every cut was centred pixel by pixel in a magnified grid. But it is the expected answer, a bookmark with a play in it, so it sits close to Play Books and to the 'symbol in a bookmark' pattern the first round was rejected for. The bleed is the only new move, and on dark wallpapers, where the graphite tile disappears, it reads as a square-topped bookmark, so many people will never see the ribbon idea. The play centre sits 7 dp above the tile centre because the notch takes the bottom; that is right for a hanging ribbon but makes the icon slightly top-heavy next to the reference. The toolbar cuts gave up the bleed for a lip, so the idea lives only in the launcher.

candidates.title: Split ribbon
candidates.idea: The same ribbon hanging from the top edge, split down the middle by one straight slot that runs from the edge into the notch. The slot is the only negative space: it turns one bookmark into two ribbons, like a book with two markers, and two bars side by side read as pause.

The slot is 8 dp, a fifth of the width, leaving two 16 dp bars: wide enough to read as a deliberate cut and as pause, narrow enough that the outline stays one bookmark. The notch is shared, so each bar's foot slopes from its outer tip up to the slot, meeting it at y 68.6; those inner corners stay sharp, like the notch's apex. Nothing else is cut.
candidates.small: Nothing needs dropping. The cuts keep a lip of tile above the bars, 3 px at 48, 2 at 32 and 1 at 16, the smallest detail each size allows: bled to the edge, the paper bars merged with light browser toolbars, and the tile's sides with the dark slot between them read as a bold W. 48: ribbon 28 px, slot 6 px, bars 11 px, notch 9 px over 14. 32: ribbon 18 px, slot 4 px, bars 7 px, notch 6 px. 16: ribbon 8 px, slot 2 px, bars 3 px, notch 4 px at 45 degrees, so each foot is a clean three-step stair. The cuts' slots are about 9 dp, a touch wider than the master's 8, because a slot has to be an even number of pixels to stay centred. Glyph: the whole bookmark, 16 px wide with its outer round shoulders, split by a 4 px slot into two 6 px bars.
candidates.risks: Two bars are the most familiar media sign there is, so at a glance it can say pause before it says bookmark; the shared notch and the bleed keep it Shelf's. Pause says stopped for now: that suits a place kept for later, but it says listen less directly than a play. On a near-white wallpaper the paper bars merge with the background and the dark frame with the slot can read as a W or a Cyrillic Ш, the same failure the toolbar cuts' lip fixes; the launcher has no such fix without giving up the bleed. On wallpapers near graphite the bar tops look flat or arched. The launch screens need an edge to hang the ribbons from.
candidates.self_critique: The strongest idea in this territory and the one I would show Richard first. A single straight cut makes pause out of Shelf's own outline, and nothing is stamped on. It holds at every size with nothing dropped, and its cuts are the crispest of the set (soft 2.3 / 3.1 / 9.1 percent against the reference's 3.5 / 6.3 / 14.7). What still bothers me: at a glance it says pause before it says bookmark, so a viewer could take it for a media app, and only the shared notch argues otherwise. I chose an 8 dp slot over 6 for a clearer pause; 6 would put the bookmark first, and I'm not certain I chose right. On a near-white wallpaper the launcher can read as a W, and the lip that fixes this in the toolbar can't be used in the launcher without giving up the bleed. The bar tops arch in the circle mask, like two tombstones on a dark wallpaper.

The notch and the safe circle take the bottom of the ribbon, so even at 46 dp wide the play crowds the top edge and the pause is only 10 dp tall. At the 1x home-screen preview the pause is a smudge, and every cut and the glyph drop it, which makes the small sizes r1 with a bigger play. Of the three it is the most media-like: a play/pause toggle in a bookmark. I nearly replaced it, but every replacement I drew in this territory was weaker or duplicated r2. Its main value is showing Richard what his three-level idea costs inside a ribbon.

dropped.dropped:
Stencil (the suggested n2): pause bars crossing the play and joining the bookmark at its top and bottom edges. I drew eleven proportions over three rounds: thin and thick bars, narrow and wide gaps, bars on the incircle and pushed towards the tip, rounded and crisper pieces, equilateral and notch-angle plays. The play always survives, but the pause never reads. The bridges are never enclosed by dark, so the eye takes them as ground rather than figure, and their ends dissolve into the paper; the dark pieces read instead as 'D | play', a skip or next-track glyph, or a play with speed lines. Replaced by the bookmark window (n2).

Inverting pause: whole bars that run past the play's edges, so the even-odd rule makes them dark slots in the paper and light bars inside the play. It is striking large and reads as a bookmark with a pause when small, but the bars cut the rounded play into a D-shaped piece and a tip, so the play stops reading. At 48 px it becomes a striped blob, and it drifts out of the nested territory into inversion.

Split-bookmark pause: the island drawn as a small Shelf bookmark split down its axis (pausing keeps your place). At 9 dp wide the slanted ends read as chamfered bars, weaken the pause and vanish at every small size: a hidden detail with no payoff.

Play drawn with the bookmark's own corners (shoulder radius at the back, tail-tip radius at the point): it sharpens the play towards the sharp triangles the first round was faulted for.

n3 variants:
- Every wall on the module, so the left wall and both bars make three equal stripes: the play slides down and left and looks off-centre.
- A 5 dp module: squashes the bars into two squares that read as a face.
- The first 4.5 dp module: gave blocky 4.5 x 10.9 bars and did not match the cuts' proportions. Superseded by 4.1 dp, which fixes both.
- A 32 px cut one pixel shorter: freed the tile corners but left squat 2 x 5 bars.

n1 and n2 variants:
- An even-gap pause pushed against the flat side: crowds it; the incircle placement looks more centred.
- Plays with 7 to 8.5 dp walls and a looser ring: starve the pause to 2.2 x 7 dp bars.
- The window placed high in the body: leaves a dead slab of paper under it.
- The window with its pause on the bookmark's axis above the notch apex: makes the play look pushed right.

At 16 px, a bigger stepped play with 1 px walls for n3 sits lopsided, so all three share one 16 px drawing (a 4 x 7 px stepped play in a 10 x 12 px bookmark). A brute-force search for an even-walled play was abandoned as too slow; my estimate is that it comes out almost exactly equilateral and box-centred, which the n1 placement tests already cover.

Sketched in a scratch harness, judged at 360 px and at real home-screen sizes, then dropped:
1. One continuous cut, the suggested p3, tried three ways: the play opening out of the notch's apex; a slot from the apex up into a centred play; the notch's right edge running on as a channel into the play's lower corner. All three turn the bookmark into a letterform (a flag on a pole, a P or an R) and split the left tail off as a prong, so the tail stops reading as a tail. Making the hole merely touch the apex at a point would break the 3 px wall rule at 48 px.
2. Hidden play: the notch's two edges, extended past the apex, already enclose a play-shaped region in the lower left with its tip on the apex. Its inradius is about 6 units, too small to hold a hole with real walls, and it sits off-centre. Its geometry became p2's construction instead.

On craft this round fixes most of what sank the last one. Every candidate has hand-drawn 48, 32 and 16 px cuts and a glyph, and the bookmark is Shelf's own (t1 and t2 change its proportions and say so). Every master except the deliberate ribbon bleeds sits inside the safe circle, and every 48 and 32 px cut holds its 3 and 2 px minimums. The pixel grid sorts the ideas. The straight vertical cuts (s1, s2, r2) are crisper than the solid reference at every size: 2.3 to 2.8% soft at 48 against 3.5. Every play hole roughly doubles the reference (7 to 10% at 48, 10 to 12.6% at 32), because a 30 or 32.9 degree edge never lands on whole pixels, and i1's disc is the softest drawing (11.6 and 17.7%). Two faults repeat. First, n1, n2, n3 and r3 share a stepped 4 x 7 px play at 16 px whose bottom pixel touches the notch's apex corner to corner, so the hole leaks into the notch; p1's 5/3/3/1 play with 2 px clear is the fix. Second, the nested pauses in n1, n2 and r3 are 2.5 to 3.5 dp, under the 4.5 dp that 3 px on a 1x home screen needs, and are dropped from every cut, so Richard's third level exists only above about 64 px (only n3 and i1 carry it to 32). Corner radii went three ways: the shoulder radius applied to 60 degree corners, which reads softer than the shoulders; p1's setback-matched radius; and p2, r1 and h1 matching the tips by angle. The round should settle on one, and p2's rule is the most defensible. metrics.json reports 0% soft for every glyph because the measure skips pixels with alpha under 250, which on a transparent glyph are exactly the soft ones; counted from alpha they run 6 to 25% (the reference is 8%). Two directions nobody tried. First, a size ladder that keeps the reference's solid bookmark at 16 px and brings the hole in from 32 up: the honest answer for any second symbol smaller than 6 px at 16. Second, a play drawn as whole-pixel stairs at 32 as well as 16, since 32 is where every play hole is softest and at 2x those steps are single device pixels.

Through Richard's brief and Shelf's brand, this round fixes what sank round one. Every option starts from Shelf's own bookmark, every small size is drawn on its own grid (all at or under the reference's 14.7% soft pixels at 16 px), and the geometry is measured. Its weakness is convergence: 8 of the 18 options are a bookmark with a play hole, a few dp apart. Richard should see three directions: p2 (the simplest answer, with the play cut at the notch's angle, which is also the angle of the play button in Shelf's player), n1 (his own nest, which reads on a real Pixel even though the 1x sheets turn its pause to specks) and s1 (the purest negative space, the bookmark cut into a pause). I expect him to pick n1 or p2, with s1 the one that could surprise him. He will think the options that break the brief's fixed points miss the point: t1 and t2 turn the bookmark on its side and deepen its notch, i1 and i2 make the bookmark a dark hole, r1 to r3 trade the square shoulders for the launcher's mask (an arch in a Pixel's default circle and on Android 12's launch screen), and h1 and h2 break the bookmark into fragments. Two directions are missing. Nobody drew the nest with Shelf's own play and pause (Lucide's 14:18 play, bars about 2.5 times their gap); n1's refinement should. And nobody tried motion: Android 12's launch screen can animate the icon, so play-then-pause can live there (the notch folding up into p2's play, then a pause rising inside it) and in the player's play-and-pause morph, leaving the static icon at two levels as simplicity asks. One context needs checking for every play option: the extension's toolbar button only saves (its spec puts any reading or listening out of scope), so a play in its 16 and 32 px cuts promises listening it does not offer. Those cuts may be better as the solid bookmark.
