The play is the notch's two cuts folded forward: its edges are parallel to the notch and as long. At 32.9° it is also the angle of the play button in Shelf's own player (Lucide, 32.7°), so the icon's play and the app's play are one shape. Two parts and drawable from memory; corners at the tips' radius give one corner language with the tail. The play survives at 48, 32 and 16 px and in the glyph. On the lock-screen media card the glyph reads as a badge beside the real pause button.
brief.fails: It sits low. Its axis is at y 52.4, 4.5 dp below the middle of the body (top 28.5 to notch apex 67.3) and 2.3 dp below p1's, with its lower-left corner level with the apex. That leaves 11.7 dp of paper above it against a 6.25 dp strap below. At 1x it looks as if it has slipped, the optical-centring fault Richard rejected in round one. The 16 px play ends in a 2 px flat tip (column 9, rows 6 to 7) that blunts it into a tab. It shares Google Play Books' pairing of bookmark and play, though only in idea.
brief.fix: Raise the play 2 dp (axis to about y 50.4). The paper above drops to about 9.7 dp and the strap along the notch grows to about 7.9 dp, so the play sits in the body above the apex and keeps the notch rhyme. At 16 px end the play on one pixel (columns of 5, 3, 3 and 1 from x 6, as in p1's cut). My first choice to refine and show.

concept.works: Richard's own idea, drawn faithfully and well. The bookmark leads, the play is the tile showing through, and the pause is the bookmark's paper again: one colour and real holes. Of the five nests (n1, n2, n3, r3, i1) it keeps the most bookmark while the play is still unmistakable at 48 px, so it is the version of his idea to show him.
concept.fails: Three symbols stacked, so it is two ideas stuck together. A play holding a pause is the play/pause toggle, which says media player at launcher size, and the pause is gone below 64 px. Every smaller size is a bookmark with a play: GoodLinks' template (a white notched bookmark with a symbol in its body, in Shelf's own category, Apple-only) and Play Books' pair of signs nested the other way. It is moderately close to both. The play is equilateral with 5.1 dp corners, about 13% of its height, the softness of Play Books' triangle (about 11%), and nothing in its shape comes from the bookmark.
concept.fix: Bring n3's play geometry into n1: slanted edges parallel to the notch (the 11:17 slope n3 and p2 use), with n1's walls kept at 6 dp or more. Hole and tail then look cut by one hand without n3's thin frame. If it still reads as Google Play, try the tips' radius on the play's back corners, as p2 does. Show it with its two-level small sizes beside it, so Richard sees the pause appears only on the launcher and the launch screens.

craft.works: Shelf's proportions at the largest size the circle allows (43.6 dp, reach 32.56). The frame round the play is close to even: 6.1 above, 6.0 over the notch, 8.3 at the flat side and 7.4 past the tip. The pause sits exactly on the incircle centre (51.5, 48.5). The 48 and 32 cuts are real redraws with 4 to 5 px walls.
craft.fails: The pause ring is 6.2 dp at the flat side against 4.0 at the slanted sides, so the bars crowd the play's edges. Bars of 3.5 dp and a 3.0 dp gap are 2.3 and 2.0 px on a 1x home screen, under the 3 px minimum. Every cut and the glyph drop the pause, so the third level exists only above about 64 px. The play's corners are r 5.1 on 60 degree angles, setting each curve back 8.8 dp against the shoulders' 5.1, so the play reads softer than the bookmark. The 48 px cut is 9.7% soft, 2.8 times the reference. At 16 px the play's bottom pixel (6,10) touches the notch's 80%-dark apex pixel (7,11) corner to corner, so the hole leaks into the notch.
craft.fix: Move the pause 1.5 dp left (centre x 50.0) to even the ring at 4.7 dp. Set the play's corners to r 3.0 dp. Redraw the 16 px play 5 px tall on rows 4 to 8 (5/3/3/1) to keep 2 px above the apex. Even then it is a weaker n3.

brief.works: Richard's own idea, drawn properly: Shelf's bookmark at 43.5 dp (reach 32.6), a play hole with 6 to 8.2 dp of paper round it, and the paper pause centred on the play's incircle (51.5, 48.5), so nothing floats. On his Pixel the launcher draws the 72 dp at about 140 px, where the pause bars are about 7 × 22 px and read clearly (checked in a scratch render); the 1x sheets understate it. He will recognise it at once and is the most likely to pick it.
brief.fails: Four parts, the busiest of the bookmark-first options. The play (38 of the bookmark's 52 dp) is louder than the bookmark, so at a glance it is a play-and-pause button in a bookmark frame, which reads as a media player. The play is the generic soft one: equilateral, corners r 5.1 (13% of its height), YouTube's shape rather than Shelf's own narrower Lucide play. The pause bars are thin sticks with a gap almost as wide as a bar (3.42 and 3.08 dp); Shelf's in-app pause (filled, 1.75 stroke) has bars about 2.5 times its gap. The pause exists only on the launcher and launch screens. Every cut and the glyph is a plain play, so in most places n1 is p1.
brief.fix: Redraw the play as Shelf's, keeping its 38.3 dp height: depth 0.78 of the height (Lucide's 14:18), edges parallel to the notch (32.9°, Lucide's 32.7°), corners at the tips' radius (about 1.9 dp). The narrower play adds about 1.6 dp of paper on each side. Give the pause Shelf's proportions in the same footprint: bars about 4 × 11.4 dp with a 1.8 dp gap, re-centred on the new incircle. The two shortlisted play options then differ only by the pause and the play's size, a clean A/B for Richard.

concept.works: Clean and centred, bookmark first, with the play legible at every size.
concept.fails: p2 with less reason behind it. The equilateral play takes nothing from the bookmark, and its 3.1 dp corners (11% of its height) are Play Books' softness. It has the same GoodLinks template and Play Books pair as p2, moderately close to both.
concept.fix: Drop in favour of p2's notch-parallel play folded into n1.

craft.works: The best-drawn play hole. Walls are 11.4 at the flat side, 10.7 past the tip, 10.2 above and 8.0 to the notch. The corner radius of r 3.1 dp on the play's 60 degree corners sets each curve back 5.4 dp, matching the shoulders' 5.0, so play and bookmark have one softness. Every cut keeps an even frame: 7 px at 48, 5 at 32, 3 at 16 and 4 in the glyph. The 16 px play (columns 5/3/3/1) floats with 2 px above and 2 px over the apex, so it doesn't leak.
craft.fails: It is the stamped symbol the brief names as the last round's failure, drawn well: the hole carries a symbol and does no other work. The diagonals double the reference's softness (7.3 / 10.4% against 3.5 / 6.3 at 48 / 32). At 16 px the 5-pixel play is at the limit of legibility. It overlaps p2 almost completely at toolbar sizes.
craft.fix: Fold its two best decisions into p2: the 16 px play (5/3/3/1 on rows 4 to 8), and the setback-matched r 3.1 dp corners if p2's crisp corners fight the shoulders. Drawn as it is, it needs no geometric fix.

brief.works: The most evenly framed play: equilateral, its flat side 0.42 of its depth left of the centre line so the walls read even (11.25 and 10.56 dp), its axis at y 50.1 on the visual centre. Two parts, bookmark first, and the play is kept at every size.
brief.fails: The play is the generic soft one (equilateral, corners r 3.1, 11% of its height): the media-player play rather than Shelf's narrower Lucide play. The even frame makes it a button set into the bookmark, the stamped reading the brief warns about. p2 does the same job with a play that belongs to Shelf.
brief.fix: Merge into p2: keep p1's placement (axis about y 50) and use p2's notch-parallel play.

concept.works: The best-integrated nest. The play's sides run parallel to the notch, one 4.1 dp module sets every wall, bar and gap, and the pause survives to 32 px. It is the only nest where Richard's third level reaches the toolbar.
concept.fails: The hole is so large that the bookmark becomes an outline frame, and an outlined bookmark is the 'not saved' state in Lucide and Material, the opposite of Shelf's first message. The play and pause read before the bookmark. Of the nests that makes it the closest to Play Books, a big soft play with a bookmark around it (Play Books' pair with the nesting swapped, moderate to close), and to a media-player button.
concept.fix: Fold it into n1. Keep its notch-parallel play and its one-module discipline, and thicken the walls to at least 6 dp (the play drops to about 38 dp tall) so the bookmark reads solid.

craft.works: The most rigorous nest. One 4.1 dp module sets the top wall, the band over the notch, both bars, the gap and the ring. The play's sides run parallel to the notch at 11:17, and the pause sits 1.9 dp left of the incircle so the ring is an even 4.1 on all three sides. It is the only nest whose cuts carry the pause: 3 px bars, gap and ring at 48, 2 px at 32, with play and notch on matching 2:3 stairs.
craft.fails: Every dimension sits on the floor. The 4.1 dp module is 2.7 px on a 1x home screen, under 3. The 48 cut is 3 px everything and the 32 cut 2 px everything, so both are busy, at 9.3 and 12.6% soft. The frame is 4.2 dp at the top against 7.0 at the sides, so the bookmark becomes an outline round a play. Play corners at r 5.1 on 57 and 66 degree angles set back 9.4 and 7.9 dp, far softer than the shoulders and the sharp apex. The 48 and 32 bookmarks fill two thirds of the tile against the master's 60%. At 16 px the play's bottom pixel (6,10) touches the notch's 80%-dark apex pixel (7,11) corner to corner, so the hole leaks into the notch.
craft.fix: If a nest goes to Richard, refine this one. Take about 0.9 dp off the play's height so the top wall and the band over the notch reach 4.5 dp. Set the play's corners to r 3 dp. Redraw the 16 px play 5 px tall with 2 px clear of the apex. Accept that the bars, gap and ring can't reach 4.5 dp inside a 43.5 dp bookmark.

brief.works: The best-built nest: the play is cut at the notch's angle and one 4.1 dp module sets every wall, bar and gap, so the pause survives down to the 32 px cut.
brief.fails: The hole takes so much that the bookmark becomes a 4.1 dp frame (2.7 px at 1x), and in most interfaces an outlined bookmark means not saved. The pause sits against the flat side, 1.9 dp left of the incircle's centre, so pause-then-point reads as the play/pause media toggle before it reads as a bookmark. The 48 and 32 px cuts draw the bookmark at two thirds of the tile, a size up from the launcher.
brief.fix: Fold its notch-parallel play and its module into n1's refinement, and drop it as a separate option.

concept.works: The most original idea in the round, and the only one no competitor resembles. One straight cut, continuing the notch's own right edge, shows that the bookmark's left tail was a play all along. It is one idea with nothing stamped on and the outline untouched: the hidden-arrow kind of discovery that makes a mark ownable.
concept.fails: The band runs edge to edge, from the left side at y 53.5 down to the right tip. That is the top-left to bottom-right direction of the 'off' slash (Tabler's bookmark-off, Lucide's bell-off), so a first reading can be 'bookmark removed', the opposite of saved. The cut also swallows the notch: the V that identifies Shelf's bookmark is gone, and the shape reads as a flag or a dog-eared page first. The play (23 x 18 dp, bottom left) reads as a media-file badge at 1x and is six pixels at 16 px. It is hard to draw from memory: which tail, and which way?
concept.fix: Test before refining: show the 48 px icon cold to five people. If 'crossed out' or 'turned off' comes up, drop it, because any edge-to-edge diagonal carries that convention. If it survives, end the cut 4.5 dp (3 px at 48) short of the left edge, so a paper hinge keeps the outline closed and the cut reads as a fold, then check the play still reads.

craft.works: The most exact construction in the round. One cut carries the notch's right flank straight on through the apex to the left edge, and the play's lower edge is the notch's own left flank. That makes the play isosceles at 0.77 (Lucide's is 0.78), and every corner except the shoulders takes the tips' r 1.853. The outline is the reference bookmark exactly. The cuts are the crispest of any idea with a diagonal: 2.2% soft at 16, where the cut, the notch and a 6/4/2 play are all whole-pixel 45 degree stairs, and 5.1 / 8.5% at 48 / 32. The play survives everywhere: 14 x 11 px at 48, 9 x 7 at 32, 7 x 6 in the glyph.
craft.fails: The cut is 3.2 dp, 2.1 px on a 1x home screen and under the 3 px minimum, so at launcher sizes it reads as a hairline slash, which is the 'bookmark off' convention. The play is a corner fragment, about 11% of the paper. At 16 px it is a 6-pixel hint that reads as a broken tail more than a play.
craft.fix: Widen the cut to 4.5 dp. Keep its upper edge on the notch's line and move the play's top edge down; the play shrinks to about 22 x 17 dp. Keep the 16 px cut's 2 px stair. Then check at 1x that the wider band reads as a fold rather than a slash.

brief.works: The cleverest geometry in the round: the outline stays whole and the play is the bookmark's own left tail.
brief.fails: The idea needs explaining. At a glance a diagonal through a bookmark is the bookmark-off slash or a folded corner, and the play is a fragment falling out of the bottom left. At 16 px it is a slash, and nobody could draw it from memory.

concept.works: Restraint: the bookmark clearly leads and the play is a quiet aside.
concept.fails: The closest of all to GoodLinks: a small dark symbol centred in a solid notched bookmark, at about the size and position of GoodLinks' star. At 6.6% of the bookmark's area the play vanishes on a 1x home screen and in the status bar, so the listen message is mostly lost.
concept.fix: Drop. A smaller stamp is still a stamp.

craft.works: Clean and restrained. The play is 6.6% of the bookmark, with walls of 15.6 at the flat side, 14.5 at the tip and above, and 9.8 to the notch, set close to the optical centre. It is the crispest of the play holes (5.3 / 8.6 / 11.9% soft). At 16 px the play is a 5/3/1 stair centred by its centroid on the bookmark's axis.
craft.fails: The play is about 10 px tall at 48 and 7 at 32, so on a 1x home screen it is a dot. At 16 px it sits on rows 5 to 9, with 3 px of paper above and 1 px over the apex. In the glyph it has 5 px above and 2 below. Both sit 1 px low.
craft.fix: Lift the 16 px play to rows 4 to 8 (2 px above, 2 over the apex) and the glyph's play by 1 px. Beyond that it is p1 at two thirds the size: a quieter option with no new idea.

brief.works: The bookmark stays the hero, with Lucide's 14:18 play at its own proportions. It is the quietest play option, the most at home beside Shelf's ink-and-paper interface, with crisp cuts (5.3% soft at 48).
brief.fails: The hole is 6.6% of the bookmark, too small for the negative space to do work. It reads as a badge on the bookmark, the clip-art reading. On a busy home screen the listening cue is a dot, and since Richard asked for negative space he is likely to find it timid.
brief.fix: If the quiet route is wanted, grow the play from 18.75 to about 22 dp tall, with p2's notch-parallel edges, at the visual centre. It then meets refined p2, so show only one of the two.

concept.works: It says saved instantly and is the simplest mark possible. Its silhouette also stands apart from the monochrome reading apps it will sit beside, which are all letterforms or abstract marks: Matter's M, Readwise Reader's R, Instapaper's I, ElevenReader's fan.
concept.fails: Nothing about listening and nothing ownable. A solid bookmark is Material's stock 'bookmark' glyph, and on a home screen it is moderately close to Day One, a white notched bookmark on a solid tile that is on Android too (Day One's bleeds off the top and is narrower).
concept.fix: None. Keep it beside the shortlist as the control: a candidate that doesn't add meaning without also adding a lookalike should lose to it on simplicity.

craft.works: The control, and per pixel the cleanest drawing: 24 x 30 at 48, 16 x 20 at 32, 8 x 10 at 16 with a 4 px 45 degree notch, and a 14 x 18 glyph. Soft 3.5 / 6.3 / 14.7%, reach 30.7 dp, clean in every mask, the themed icon and both launch screens.
craft.fails: It has no second idea and no negative space, so it can't answer the brief. It also leaves size unused: 40.2 dp wide against the 42 to 43.6 dp the candidates reach inside the same circle.
craft.fix: Keep it on Richard's page as the baseline beside the shortlist. Use its cuts (whole-pixel shoulders, the 4 px notch) as the template for every shortlisted 16 px cut and glyph.

brief.works: Shelf's bookmark exactly (today's foreground.svg scaled 1.18, 40.2 × 48.1 dp, reach 30.7): one part, drawable from memory, crisp cuts (3.5, 6.3 and 14.7% soft), already the dark launch screen's shape, and the quietest neighbour for Shelf's ink-and-paper interface.
brief.fails: It answers none of what Richard asked for: no negative space and no hint of listening. At 1x a white bookmark on black is the generic bookmarks icon, kept Shelf's only by the square shoulders and the shallow notch.
brief.fix: Nothing to fix as an answer. Keep it on the page as the control every option must beat, and as the fallback if Richard decides a listening cue is not worth a hole.

concept.works: The bleed adds a real second idea: the tile is the book and the ribbon marks your place, a strong picture of coming back to something.
concept.fails: That picture is Day One's icon: a white ribbon hanging off the top edge of its tile, with a shallow notch, and Day One is on Android. r1 is Day One with a play hole, so the likeness is close. A ribbon hanging from an edge with a play is also Play Books' own device (its ribbon hangs inside the play's top edge), and the play here is stamped. The bleed costs Shelf's shoulders and needs a lip of tile on pale wallpapers and toolbars.

craft.works: A well-placed play: edges parallel to the notch, corners at the tips' radius, walls of 11.8 / 11.1 / 10.5 dp, all far above the minimum. The cuts are clean (5.5 / 6.8 / 9.6% soft). The 16 px play is a 5/3/1 stair centred by its centroid, and a deliberate 3, 2 and 1 px lip of tile sits above the ribbon in the toolbar cuts.
craft.fails: The bleed depends on the mask and the wallpaper. Under the circle and teardrop the ribbon's top is cut into an arch. On a light home screen the paper runs into the wallpaper and the tile reads as a dark U round a bookmark-shaped opening. The launch screens, and Android 12's circle-masked splash, need an edge for it to hang from. The toolbar cuts need a lip the master doesn't have, so the family has two drawings of the top. Without the bleed it is p1.
craft.fix: Keep it only if Richard wants the tile-as-book reading, and test the 1x light home screen and the circle mask with him first. Otherwise fold its play (parallel to the notch, r 1.76) into p2.

brief.works: A good idea: the tile becomes the book and the bookmark its ribbon marker. The play's edges run parallel to the notch with even 10.5 to 11.8 dp walls, and in the rounded-square mask it looks lovely.
brief.fails: The ribbon runs off the top, so Shelf's square shoulders are replaced by whatever the mask is. In a Pixel's default circle the top becomes an arch about 6 dp high, and on a dark wallpaper the tile's edge disappears, so the arch reads as the bookmark's own shape (checked at 140 px). Android 12's launch screen draws the icon inside a circle and cuts it the same way. The website and light launch screen have no edge to hang from, the toolbar cuts need a lip, and the glyph is the whole bookmark. That makes two drawings for one brand, against the study's one-drawing rule.
brief.fix: Its free-standing twin is p2 with r1's play, which the p2 refinement covers. Keep the ribbon only as a separate study if Richard asks for it.

concept.works: A paused bookmark carries the right meaning (stop here, come back). Leaving out the play keeps it clear of Play Books, and the slots' bottoms echo the notch.
concept.fails: It stamps a pause into the body: GoodLinks' template with a pause where the star would be. The echo is invisible below 48 px, and two vertical slots over a V read as a face, eyes over a mouth. s1 says the same thing with one cut in place of two holes.

craft.works: Careful geometry. The two 8 dp holes are the bookmark's own outline inset, with bottoms parallel to the notch, so the chevron band under them is an even 9 dp. Walls are 11.1 at the sides and 10.6 above. Every cut is on whole pixels: holes of 5, 4 and 2 px with spines of 4, 2 and 2 at 48, 32 and 16, and flat bottoms at 16. Soft 5.4 / 9.6% at 48 / 32.
craft.fails: The 4.1 dp spine is 2.7 px on a 1x home screen, under 3. At 16 px, two 2 x 5 slots over a stepped notch read as a face: two eyes and a frown. The echo disappears below 48. It is a pause stamped into the body, the construction the brief calls clip art, and s1 says pause with one cut and no face.
craft.fix: Spine 4.5 dp (holes 7.8). At 16 px drop the pause rather than draw a face. s1 makes this candidate redundant.

brief.works: Clean at launcher size, and the holes' slanted bottoms run parallel to the notch, so the paper under them is an even chevron.
brief.fails: A pause stamped into a bookmark, round one's clip-art construction. The echo is invisible below 48 px, and at 16 px two slots over the notch read as a face. A light shape with two vertical slots and a notched foot is close to Twitch's logo, a streaming app. Its glyph duplicates the pause button on the media card.
brief.fix: None; s1 makes the pause out of the bookmark itself.

concept.works: s1's split plus a second picture: a book with two ribbon markers.
concept.fails: With no shoulders the halves read as two separate bars, so pause and II come before bookmark. The light colourway, two black bars running off a paper tile, is moderately close to ElevenLabs' II. The bleed is Day One's device, and on pale wallpapers the frame reads as W or Ш, as its own notes say.
concept.fix: Drop in favour of s1, whose shoulders make the halves one bookmark.

craft.works: With s1, the crispest cuts in the round (2.3 / 3.1 / 9.1% soft). An 8 dp slot (5.3 px at 1x) becomes 6, 4 and 2 px in the cuts. Every edge is vertical, and the feet are clean stairs at 16.
craft.fails: The bleed fails worst here. On a light home screen the two paper bars merge with the wallpaper, and the dark tile with its slot reads as a Ш or a W. The circle and teardrop masks arch the tops of the bars. The 16 px needs a 1 px lip. It is s1's idea with a failure s1 doesn't have.

brief.works: s1's split on the hanging ribbon: two parts, and crisp (2.3 and 3.1% soft at 48 and 32).
brief.fails: It has all of r1's mask and launch-screen problems, and it reads as a pause first: two bars hanging from the edge. On a pale wallpaper the dark frame becomes the figure and reads as a W.
brief.fix: None; s1 is the better form of the idea.

concept.works: Literal and calm: the bookmark is the hole, and on paper it becomes a dark book with a light ribbon.
concept.fails: It is Material's stock 'book' glyph, a page with a bookmark cut out at its head, so nothing about it is ownable. It says nothing about listening, and a narrow portrait card at 26% paper reads as a phone, an e-reader or a cards app at a glance.

craft.works: The crispest drawing that has a diagonal in it: 5.0 / 5.0 / 5.8% soft, with every edge except the notch on whole pixels. One corner language: the page corners are r 3.3, the bookmark's own shoulder radius. An even 6 dp margin on three sides becomes 4, 3 and 2 px in the cuts, with 14 dp of page below the tips. The light colourway, a dark book with a light bookmark, is strong.
craft.fails: It leaves out listening on purpose, so the negative space carries no second idea. At 16 px the 10 x 14 page runs from row 1 to row 14, leaving 1 px of tile above and below, so on a light toolbar the tile turns into a hairline frame round a light card. At 26% paper it is the slightest mark on a home screen, and the ink centroid sits 3.9 dp low (57.9) because the solid page is all at the bottom.
craft.fix: At 16 px draw the page 10 x 12 on rows 2 to 13 with a 6 x 7 bookmark and a 2 px notch, so the tile keeps 2 px above and below. In the master, shorten the page from 55 to 52 dp with the margins unchanged, so the solid foot is lighter and the centroid comes up.

brief.works: Simple (two parts), crisp at every size (5.0, 5.0 and 5.8% soft) and plainly a bookmarked page.
brief.fails: The bookmark becomes a dark hole and listening is gone, so it misses both halves of Richard's ask. A light card on a dark tile reads as a phone, an e-reader or a generic bookmarked-document pictogram, and at 26% paper it looks slight beside other icons.
brief.fix: None; ref-solid already answers whether the bookmark alone carries Shelf.

concept.works: Bookmark first; the nest at its most restrained.
concept.fails: A badge set in a bookmark, which is the clip-art construction. The pause island (bars 3.3 x 10 dp) is specks at 1x, so the third level adds complexity nobody sees. GoodLinks' template plus Play Books' pair.
concept.fix: Drop. n1 holds the nest with a play big enough for its pause.

craft.works: The calmest frame of the nests (10.6 / 10.4 / 9.1 / 7.5 dp) and the most solid bookmark. The pause sits on the incircle, and the cuts are tidy (7.8 / 10.8% soft).
craft.fails: The third level is too small to exist. Bars are 3.3 x 10 dp, the gap 2.8 and the ring 3.0 at the slants: 2.2, 1.9 and 2.0 px at 1x. On a home screen the pause is two specks, and every cut and the glyph drop it, leaving a less even p1. The ring is 4.7 at the flat side against 3.0 at the slants. It has the same 16 px corner-touch leak as n1 ((6,10) to (7,11)), and the same r 5.1 play corners, softer than the shoulders.
craft.fix: Without the pause this is p1. A kept pause needs the play to grow until its bars, gap and ring are each at least 4.5 dp, which this bookmark can't hold.

brief.works: The bookmark reads before the play, with 7.5 to 10.4 dp of paper round the hole.
brief.fails: The pause is jammed into the play with a 3 dp ring (bars 3.3 × 10 dp), so the island looks stamped on and becomes specks below 64 px. It is n1 with less of everything. Its own designer calls it a play badge placed on a bookmark, the clip-art reading round one was rejected for.
brief.fix: Not worth fixing: n1 carries the nest. If a smaller play is wanted, drop the pause and it becomes the p family.

concept.works: A smart inversion that gives the light colourway Richard's solid bookmark, and 'a bookmark is a pause in reading' is a good line.
concept.fails: On a home screen it is a white disc holding two bars, the generic circular pause button the brief rules out, and the brightest icon on the screen at 42% paper. A light disc filling a dark tile with dark marks inside is Spotify's layout (moderate), and a disc holding a media symbol is YouTube Music's. The light colourway, an ink disc with a paper bookmark, is Telegram's Saved Messages avatar. The disc adds no meaning, and the pause is gone at 16 px and in the glyph.
concept.fix: Drop. If the inversion is wanted, use it only as the light colourway of a bookmark-first mark.

craft.works: The only three-level mark whose master clears 4.5 dp everywhere: disc ring 5.7 at the tips, bars 5.6, gap 5.4, island ring 6.3 or more. So the pause survives to 32 px (2 px bars and gap, 4 px ring), and the 48 cut has generous 4 px bars. The bookmark is today's exact proportions. The hand-stepped 16 px disc is crisp (6.5%).
craft.fails: The disc can't sit on the grid: 11.6% soft at 48 and 17.7% at 32, against the reference's 3.5 and 6.3, and the glyph is 25% soft counted from alpha. On the circle mask the 32 dp disc leaves a 4 dp dark ring (2.7 px at 1x) that reads as an outline round a white button. At 42% paper it is the brightest mark on a dark home screen. The pause is gone at 16 and in the glyph, leaving a bookmark in a disc.
craft.fix: Drop. Its lesson for any nest is that the third level needs bars and gaps of 5.5 dp or more, which only this inversion found room for.

brief.works: A real three-level figure-ground drawing that uses only two radii.
brief.fails: It inverts Richard's ask: the bookmark is dark and the paper is a disc. The icon becomes a white circle, 42% paper against the reference's 33%: the brightest icon on a dark home screen and a white flash on the dark launch screen. In the circle mask the tile vanishes. It reads as a round button or Telegram's Saved Messages, and it has four parts.

concept.works: The purest negative-space idea in the round: no holes at all, and the play is the space the bookmark's own notch leaves open.
concept.fails: On its side it stops being a bookmark. A horizontal slab with a chevron bite reads as a tag, a ticket, a '>' prompt (Termux's >_ on black) or Plex's chevron before it reads as a play, and the play needs pointing out. The notch was deepened from 11/34 to 14/18 of the width, so even the bookmark's proportions are gone. It fails the first test, saved first.
concept.fix: Drop the rotation. Its question, whether the notch itself can be the play, deserves another try with the bookmark upright; h1 is the nearest answer so far.

craft.works: One solid shape with no holes, so it is about as crisp as the reference (4.6 / 7.8 / 14.7% soft) and nothing has to be dropped at any size. The apex takes the shoulder radius, so the play-shaped wedge is as soft as the shoulders. Inside safe at 32.6.
craft.fails: It breaks the fixed bookmark. The notch goes from 11/34 to 14/18 of the width (0.32 to 0.78, 2.4 times deeper) and the mark lies on its side, so the hang and the shallow, chunky tail that make it Shelf's are gone. At every size it reads as a tag, a pennant or a > prompt. The prongs end in single soft pixels at 48 and 16.
craft.fix: Nothing within the brief: restoring the 11/34 notch kills the play, and that is the finding.

brief.works: One solid shape with no holes, and using the notch as the play is a genuinely clever thought.
brief.fails: It is no longer Shelf's bookmark. On its side, with the notch deepened from 0.32 to 0.78 of the width, it reads as a tag, a label or a terminal prompt (Plex's chevron, Gmail's important marker). The play is a bite open to the tile, so most people will see a chevron first. Richard asked to keep his bookmark, so he will think it misses the point.

concept.works: Richard's three levels, with more room for the pause than a free-standing bookmark gives.
concept.fails: Day One's ribbon plus Play Books' pair plus the play/pause toggle. The 10 dp pause is gone below the launcher, so the third level costs the most for the least.

craft.works: The ribbon's extra width (46 dp) gives the play 31 dp of height with walls of 12.3, 11.6 and 8 dp. The cuts drop the pause honestly and keep a clean play.
craft.fails: The smallest third level in the round. Bars are 3.3 x 10.2 dp, the gap 2.7 and the ring 2.4 to 2.7 dp, about 2.2, 1.8 and 1.6 px at 1x: a smudge on any home screen, and gone from every cut and the glyph, which are then r1 with a bigger play. The 16 px 4 x 7 play's bottom pixel (6,9) touches the notch's 70%-dark apex pixel (7,10) corner to corner. r1's bleed problems apply.
craft.fix: Drop. If the nest belongs anywhere, it belongs in n3.

brief.works: It gives Richard's third level the most room by giving up the shoulders.
brief.fails: The pause is 10.2 dp tall with a 2.4 dp ring: a smudge at 1x and gone from every cut, so in most places this is r1 with a bigger play. The play sits 10 to 11.5 dp under the mask's top, crowding the arch. Of all the options it leans furthest towards a media app, and it has r1's bleed problems.
brief.fix: None; n1 does the three levels better.

concept.works: Clever geometry: the play exists only where the two saves overlap. Two bookmarks also hint at a collection, the nearest anything here comes to the name Shelf.
concept.fails: At a glance it is three pieces (a bookmark, a bar and a triangle beneath), and the play reads as a symbol dropped under the front bookmark, where it should read as an overlap. Two overlapping bookmarks is Material's stock 'bookmarks' glyph. The play is gone at 16 px, and the glyph is crowded at 18 px.
concept.fix: Drop as drawn. Carry the 'saves standing side by side' thought into a round about the name.

craft.works: A clever overlap. With the back bookmark half a width right and one notch lower, the front one's right flank cuts a play from the back one's corner, at Lucide's 0.77 with corners at the tips' radius. The cuts hold 3 px gaps at 48 and 2 px at 32.
craft.fails: Three pieces of paper and two 2.5 dp gaps, 1.7 px at 1x and under the minimum. Each bookmark is 31 dp, the smallest in the round. The 17 x 13 dp play reads at small sizes as a symbol placed under the front bookmark, and its origin as a second bookmark's corner needs a second look. The 16 px cut drops the play and becomes an 8 x 9 bookmark with a 2 px notch beside a 3 px bar. Two overlapping bookmarks is Material's 'bookmarks' glyph.
craft.fix: No fix survives the sizes; drop.

brief.works: Both bookmarks stay whole and the play appears where they overlap.
brief.fails: Three pieces, with a 17 dp play tucked under the front tail: busy, and it needs a second look. Two overlapping bookmarks is Material's generic bookmarks glyph. Each bookmark is only 31 dp wide, so the mark looks small on a home screen, and the 16 px cut loses the play.

concept.works: Both of Richard's symbols are negative space in one solid shape.
concept.fails: It is the play/pause symbol drawn as a slab: a media remote before a reading app, with the bookmark reduced to a frame around two controls. In the light colourway a dark horizontal slab holding a light play is YouTube's structure, though only weakly. It also inherits t1's sideways problem.

craft.works: Tidy pixel work: slots of 5/3/5 px at 48, 3/2/3 at 32 and 2/2/2 in the glyph, with 3 to 4 px walls, all on whole pixels. The 16 px cut honestly drops the pause.
craft.fails: It has t1's broken proportions, plus a play beside a pause, which is the media toggle the brief warns against: the bookmark becomes the frame round two transport symbols. At 16 px it falls back to t1.

brief.works: Both of Richard's symbols are negative space in one solid shape.
brief.fails: Play beside pause is the universal media toggle, so it reads as a remote or music app before a reading app. The bookmark has gone (sideways, deep notch), and the 16 px cut falls back to t1.

concept.works: A useful study of how far a slot can rise before the bookmark breaks.
concept.fails: It reads as neither a bookmark nor a pause, more like a Π, a gate, trousers or rocket fins, as its own notes say.

craft.works: Pixel-perfect: the slot is axis-aligned, so the cuts are 2.6 / 4.6 / 10.2% soft, crisper than the reference, and Shelf's outline is untouched.
craft.fails: By its own designer's account the slot carries no second idea. A 6.3 dp slot rising 17.5 dp from the apex reads as a split tail, a Π, an inverted Y or rocket fins, and at 16 px it is a 2 x 4 px stub under the head. The negative space does no work.
craft.fix: No fix is worth making. Its finding, that any bridge across the top kills the pause, is why s1 cuts all the way through.

brief.works: Shelf's bookmark is kept, and it shows how deep a slot can go.
brief.fails: It carries no second idea: neither pause nor play. As its designer says, it reads as a split tail, a Π, trousers or rocket fins.
